question: A team wants its fact-checking of Claude outputs to be reviewable by someone else months later. Which practice best achieves that?
options: A) Keep the full chat transcript, since it shows every single question the team put to Claude.
B) Record which claims were checked and against what, and keep that alongside the document.
C) Have a second person read the finished document and confirm that it reads correctly.
D) Add a standard line to the document stating that all claims in it have been verified.
correct_answers: B) Record which claims were checked and against what, and keep that alongside the document.
explanations: Incorrect. A transcript shows how the draft was produced but not which claims were subsequently checked or against which sources.
Correct. A record of coverage lets a later reviewer see what was verified and what was not, instead of having to redo the work or assume it was done.
Incorrect. A readability pass does not establish that any statement was traced to a source.
Incorrect. An unsupported assurance is not reviewable, and it obscures which claims were actually examined.
